subject: a problem about different line types in ggplot

messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: a problem about different line types in ggplot
parts:
Hi ggplot users,

I have a problem to show different groups. For example, there are two datasets with the same structure.

DF1
time               var1     var2
2007-01-01    0.1       0.2
2007-02-01    0.5       0.3
2007-03-01    0.6       0.2
2007-04-01    0.5       0.1
...

DF2
time               var1     var2
2007-01-01    0.3       0.5
2007-02-01    0.2       0.6

I use the code below to show var1 from the two dataframes in one figure, but it does not help. Could anyone tell me how to correct it, and to show one solid line and one dashed line in the figure? Thanks a lot.

figure1 = ggplot()+
  geom_line(data=DF1, aes(x=time, y=var1, linetype=1))+ theme_bw()+
  geom_line(data=DF2, aes(x=time, y=var1, linetype=2))
print(figure1)

The error message is:
Error: A continuous variable can not be mapped to linetype

If I do like this, there is just one solid line:
figure1 = ggplot()+
  geom_line(data=DF1, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=1)+ theme_bw()+
  geom_line(data=DF2, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=2)+
print(figure1)

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: a problem about different line types in ggplot
parts:
figure1 = ggplot()+
geom_line(data=DF1, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=1)+ theme_bw()+
geom_line(data=DF2, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=2)

print(figure1)

works for me, but what is the meaning of the solid vs dashed line?
Usually something like

DF <- rbind(data.frame(DF1, source = "DF1"),
data.frame(DF2, source = "DF2"))

ggplot(DF,
mapping = aes(x = time, y = var1, linetype = source)) +
geom_line()

makes more sense.

Best,
Ista

On Wed, May 10, 2017 at 1:33 PM, lily li <choc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> It does not work for me. There is just one solid line in the figure. I meant
> to have one variable in DF1 show as solid line, the other variable in DF2
> show as dashed line.

Are you sure? Note that your original code had a typo (extra "+" at
the end of the plotting code) that I corrected. Try running exactly
this:

library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
DF1 <- read.table(text = "time var1 var2

2007-04-01 0.5 0.1",
header = TRUE)
DF2 <- read.table(text = "time var1 var2
2007-01-01 0.3 0.5
2007-02-01 0.2 0.6",
header = TRUE)
DF1$time <- ymd(DF1$time)
DF2$time <- ymd(DF2$time)

figure1 = ggplot()+
geom_line(data=DF1, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=1) + theme_bw() +
geom_line(data=DF2, aes(x=time, y=var1), linetype=2)
print(figure1)


>

> Yes, your code works, but it needs more to type than the former one, which
> does not need to manipulate the data frame.
Sure, except that you have no legend to tell you what the line type means...

Best,
Ista
